capability_investigated:
generate(features, prompts, ...) signature and the WhisperFeatureExtractor
output shape — specifically whether the decode call accepts a batched
StorageView (N x n_mels x 3000) with a parallel prompt list rather than a
single 30s window.
what_i_learned:
The processor pads/truncates every input to a fixed 30s mel window, so the
stub silently dropped everything past the first 30 seconds of each call
(pure deletion). generate takes a list of prompts, so a batched feature
StorageView with one prompt per window decodes all segments in a single
call and returns one result per window.
hypothesis:
Split audio into ceil(len/30s) non-overlapping 30s windows, extract all
features at once, run one batched generate over [prompt]*N, and join the
per-window transcripts. This recovers the deleted tail and should sharply
raise length_ratio.p05 / cut the deletion rate that dominates the stub.

capability_investigated:
Re-examined generate()'s memory behavior on a batched StorageView: how peak
GPU allocation scales with the number of 30s windows passed in one decode
call (N x n_mels x 3000 features + N parallel beams).
what_i_learned:
generate() decodes all prompts in the list concurrently, so a single batched
call over every window of a long call allocates memory proportional to the
window count — long 0715 calls have enough windows to exceed GPU memory
(CUDA out of memory). Decoding one window per generate() call bounds peak
memory to a single 30s window and still recovers the full tail.
hypothesis:
Keep the long-form windowing that fixed the tail-deletion, but iterate the
windows through generate() one at a time instead of one giant batched call;
this removes the OOM crash while preserving the deletion fix, so the
iteration actually scores.

capability_investigated:
The WhisperGenerationResult object returned by frozen.generate() — specifically
its scores and no_speech_prob fields, and the return_scores /
return_no_speech_prob decode flags that populate them. Also the n-gram
blocking knob no_repeat_ngram_size on the decode call.
what_i_learned:
generate() exposes per-sequence avg log-prob (scores) and a per-window
no_speech_prob, but ONLY when return_scores=True / return_no_speech_prob=True
are passed — otherwise result.scores is empty and the signals are discarded.
This means coverage loss can be localized: every window IS decoded (loss isn't
at the chunker), so low length_ratio comes from individual windows collapsing
into repetition / early-EOS, detectable via low score + low unique-token ratio
while no_speech_prob stays low.
hypothesis:
Condition a fallback on those discarded signals: greedy-decode each window,
and only when its output is empty / score < -1.0 / repetitive AND
no_speech_prob < 0.6 (real speech present) re-decode once with beam_size=5 +
no_repeat_ngram_size=3 to break the loop and recover the deleted span. Targets
the dominant deletion axis without touching windows that already decode clean.

capability_investigated:
The decoder prompt fed to generate()'s `prompts` arg and Whisper's
timestamp-token vocabulary. Every prior iteration hard-coded
<|notimestamps|>, so the decode had never run in timestamped mode and the
emitted segment timestamps were never available.
what_i_learned:
Removing <|notimestamps|> from the prompt switches the backend into
timestamped decode: the returned sequences_ids carry timestamp tokens
(ids >= convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>"), spaced 0.02s), which
skip_special_tokens=True strips from the text but which can be read to find
where decoding stopped. This exposes the in-window stop position the
notimestamps regime hid, and the timestamp-trained decode is designed to walk
to the window end rather than early-EOS on long dense segments.
hypothesis:
In-window early truncation (len 0.66, del 82%) is the deletion source. Decode
each window with timestamps enabled, then advance the cursor to the last
emitted timestamp instead of a fixed 30s hop, so a window that stops early
gets its dropped tail re-decoded with context — recovering coverage at the
exact failure point, within the greedy runtime budget.

capability_investigated:
The decoder `prompts` arg fed to generate() — specifically Whisper's
previous-text context slot marked by <|startofprev|>, which precedes the
<|startoftranscript|> sot sequence. No iteration has put anything before
sot; the prompt has only ever been [sot, ko, transcribe].
what_i_learned:
generate()'s prompt token list accepts a previous-text segment before the
sot sequence: [<|startofprev|>] + prior_text_token_ids + [sot, ko,
transcribe]. Whisper conditions the decode on those prior tokens (the same
mechanism faster-whisper uses to carry context across long-form segments),
so cross-window context is an available, never-used input axis. Decoder
context is 448 tokens, bounding how much prior text can be prepended.
hypothesis:
Dominant axis is substitution (57%, coverage healthy at 0.95) → errors are
domain terms mis-recognized, and each 30s window currently decodes with zero
memory of the call. Carry the previous window's decoded text into the next
window as the <|startofprev|> prompt so the decoder is primed with running
call-center context and keeps domain vocabulary consistent across window
boundaries instead of independently re-guessing it.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return value under beam search — specifically that sequences_ids
and scores are PARALLEL N-best lists (one entry per hypothesis), populated
only when beam_size>1 / num_hypotheses>1. Every prior iter decoded greedily
(beam_size=1) and read only sequences_ids[0], so the ranked alternatives the
call can return have never existed in this pipeline.
what_i_learned:
With beam_size=5, num_hypotheses=5, return_scores=True the WhisperGeneration
result exposes up to 5 ranked hypotheses with parallel avg-log-prob scores;
greedy decoding yields a degenerate 1-entry list and discards this entirely.
This gives both a search that can back out of a locally-wrong token (the
substitution lever) and an N-best set selectable by criteria other than the
beam's own score ranking.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (57%) with coverage already healthy — greedy commits
to locally-wrong tokens on domain/phone-band audio. Enable beam search and,
among hypotheses within a small score margin of the best, keep the one
reaching furthest into the window: beam search attacks substitution while the
completeness tie-break protects coverage without rewarding hallucinated length
(the insertion regression that sank iter5). Turbo's 4-layer decoder keeps
beam 5 within the runtime budget.

capability_investigated:
ctranslate2 Whisper.generate's avg-log-prob (result.scores, length-normalized
mean log-prob) and the sampling regime (beam_size=1, sampling_topk=0,
sampling_temperature>0) versus the beam regime — i.e. using the returned
score as a decode TRIGGER rather than only as a within-decode rerank key.
what_i_learned:
ct2's result.scores entry is already the length-normalized mean log-prob, the
exact quantity Whisper's reference decoder gates temperature-fallback on, so
it is directly comparable to the -1.0 log_prob_threshold. Sampling decode is
reachable through the frozen surface via beam_size=1 + sampling_topk=0 +
sampling_temperature>0, giving a stochastic re-decode the beam regime never
produces. Every prior iter consumed scores only to rerank N-best within one
decode and never to decide whether to re-decode.
hypothesis:
Add the canonical temperature-fallback loop: a window whose temp-0 beam decode
has avg_logprob < -1.0 (low confidence = substitution) or gzip
compression_ratio > 2.4 (repetition = hallucination, the two focus files'
failure) is re-decoded by sampling at higher temperatures, keeping the first
attempt clearing both gates. This escapes a wrong path the beam committed to
(substitution lever) and catches collapsed-into-filler windows (hallucination
lever) using a signal we always discarded.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> previous-text context slot in generate()'s prompt list
(ledger iter5), but used as a CONSTANT carrier rather than rolling decoded
text — i.e. whether the slot accepts a fixed biasing vocabulary independent
of what was just transcribed, the way faster-whisper's initial_prompt /
hotwords work.
what_i_learned:
The <|startofprev|> slot is not restricted to prior decoded output: it
accepts any token sequence as a persistent decode-conditioning prefix
([sot_prev] + glossary_ids + [sot, ko, transcribe]), so a fixed domain
glossary can prime every window's token probabilities toward in-domain
spellings. This is a distinct use of the slot from iter5's cross-window
text carry, and it targets substitution (what is mis-recognized) rather than
coverage, bounded by the 448-token decoder context.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (58%, coverage healthy at 0.96), concentrated in
insurance/call-center domain terms over phone-band audio. Seeding a constant
domain glossary into the previous-text slot biases the decoder toward the
correct spelling of those terms instead of re-guessing them per window,
lowering substitution without the per-window text-carry cost or the
hallucination risk of conditioning on possibly-wrong prior output.

capability_investigated:
ctranslate2 Whisper.generate's `patience` decoding kwarg — a beam-search
termination control distinct from beam_size/num_hypotheses. The ledger covers
beam width, N-best, scores, temperature/sampling, no_repeat_ngram, but never
the patience knob that decides how long beams keep expanding before the search
stops.
what_i_learned:
generate() exposes `patience` (default 1.0) separate from beam_size: width
fixes how many beams run, patience scales how many extra expansions the beam
performs past the first num_hypotheses completions before finalizing. At
patience>1 the search can let a globally-higher-prob token sequence overtake an
earlier locally-optimal one — a search-depth lever orthogonal to the width and
penalty knobs already tried, reachable through the frozen surface with no new
return fields.
hypothesis:
Set patience=2.0 on the existing width-5 beam decode. The dominant error is
substitution with healthy coverage (len 0.96), i.e. the beam commits to
locally-wrong tokens; extending beam expansion before termination gives the
correct sequence a chance to overtake, lowering substitution without touching
coverage or adding hallucinated length.

capability_investigated:
The model object load() returns is the live ctranslate2 Whisper, so its
methods beyond generate() are reachable. Studied align(features,
start_sequence, text_tokens, num_frames) and its return type
WhisperAlignmentResult, specifically the text_token_probs field — a
per-text-token acoustic posterior. No prior iteration called any method other
than generate().
what_i_learned:
align() is callable on load()'s returned model and returns per-text-token
acoustic probabilities (text_token_probs), batched over a list of text-token
sequences for one feature window with a num_frames frame count
(~50 encoder frames/sec, 1500 for a full 30s window). This is an acoustic
confidence the beam's length-normalized avg-log-prob score does not isolate,
because that score also folds in the LM prior — so it ranks N-best
hypotheses by a signal beam scores cannot provide.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (58%) with coverage healthy, so the lever is picking
the acoustically-faithful hypothesis among near-tie beams rather than the one
the LM-influenced score prefers. Among hypotheses within _SCORE_MARGIN of the
top score, rerank by mean text_token_probs from a single batched align() call
and keep the highest; fall back to the completeness tie-break when fewer than
two hypotheses have alignable text, guarding coverage.

capability_investigated:
model.align(features, start_sequence, text_tokens, num_frames) — the batch
contract between the features StorageView and the text_tokens list, which is
what iter10 violated.
what_i_learned:
align() requires features.batch == len(text_tokens): passing a single 30s
feature window (batch 1) against an N-hypothesis text-token batch raises
"MatMul: batch dimension of inputs a and b should match". The correct usage
is faster-whisper's: one align() call per hypothesis with a 1-element
text_tokens batch against the batch-1 feature window, reading text_token_probs.
hypothesis:
Repair iter10 by calling align() per hypothesis (batch 1) instead of one
batched call over all N hypotheses. Among score-margin N-best contenders,
rerank by mean acoustic posterior; fall back to the iter_006 completeness
tie-break when fewer than two hypotheses carry alignable text. This makes the
acoustic-rerank substitution lever actually run without crashing.

capability_investigated:
How ctranslate2 Whisper.generate populates the num_hypotheses N-best slot
under the SAMPLING regime (beam_size=1, sampling_topk=0,
sampling_temperature>0) versus beam search — i.e. whether the same N-best
return surface that align() reranks can be filled with independent diverse
samples instead of beam tails.
what_i_learned:
Beam search shares a long common decode prefix across hypotheses, so the
within-margin N-best contenders that align()'s acoustic posterior reranks are
near-duplicates and the rerank rarely changes the chosen tokens. Switching the
same call to sampling (beam_size=1, sampling_topk=0, sampling_temperature>0,
num_hypotheses=N, return_scores=True) makes generate() draw N INDEPENDENT
samples that diverge specifically at low-confidence, substitution-prone tokens
— a diverse candidate pool the beam regime cannot produce — at lower cost than
the 5-beam search.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (58%) and align acoustic rerank is our best pipeline
but had near-identical beam hypotheses to choose between. Feeding align a
temperature-sampled N-best instead gives it genuinely distinct spellings of
the same audio, so it can select the acoustically-faithful domain-term token
over the LM-fluent-but-wrong one. Only the decode call changed (beam→sampling
at temp 0.4); the per-hypothesis align rerank and completeness fallback are
untouched.

capability_investigated:
The N independent hypotheses generate() returns under the sampling regime
(beam_size=1, sampling_topk=0, sampling_temperature>0, num_hypotheses=N,
return_scores=True) — iter12's diverse pool — but examined as a SET to vote
over rather than a ranked list to pick the top of. Studied how the returned
parallel sequences_ids can be consumed by a consensus rule instead of a
per-hypothesis acoustic rerank.
what_i_learned:
The substitution-attacking signal in a diverse sampling pool is not in any
single hypothesis's score or acoustic posterior (a rerank can only re-order,
never cancel an error) but in the AGREEMENT across hypotheses: when N samples
mis-hear a domain term in N different ways, the correct rendering is the modal
one. The frozen surface needs nothing new for this — sequences_ids already
carries the full pool; the consumption rule (Minimum-Bayes-Risk / medoid over
pairwise edit distance) is a pure post-process that no prior iter applied, and
it removes the per-hypothesis align() passes iter11/iter12 spent.
hypothesis:
Replace the single-best selector (align acoustic rerank) with MBR selection
over the sampling pool: decode all N hypotheses, pick the one minimizing mean
length-normalized character edit distance to the others. Because the dominant
axis is substitution (58%) of domain/phone-band tokens that each sample gets
wrong independently, the consensus pick should cancel those idiosyncratic
errors in a way a rerank cannot, lowering corpus_cer; runtime drops since
align() is gone.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_no_speech_prob decode flag and the WhisperGenerationResult.no_speech_prob
field it populates — a per-window acoustic non-speech posterior, distinct from
the avg-log-prob scores we already consume. Never requested in any prior iter,
so the field has always come back empty and been discarded.
what_i_learned:
result.no_speech_prob is populated ONLY when return_no_speech_prob=True is passed
to generate(); it is a single per-window scalar (not per-hypothesis) sitting
alongside sequences_ids/scores on the same result object. It is the exact signal
Whisper's reference decoder gates silence-skip on, and combined with the best
hypothesis' mean log-prob (already available via return_scores) it reconstructs
the canonical no_speech>0.6 AND avg_logprob<-1.0 rule with no new return surface.
hypothesis:
The two harness-flagged eval files both trip the hallucination guard (hal 0.18,
insertion 10%) — text emitted over the long near-silent windows these calls
contain (silences up to 34s). Request no_speech_prob and drop a window's text
when its no-speech posterior exceeds 0.6 AND even the best hypothesis' mean
log-prob is below -1.0, then hop a full window past it. The conjunction keeps
quiet but real speech (low score alone) from being deleted, so hallucinated
non-speech text is suppressed instead of inserted.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s decoded-text degeneracy signal — not a returned field but the
gzip compression ratio (len(utf8)/len(zlib(utf8))) of the decode, the probe
OpenAI's reference DecodingTask pairs with avg-log-prob to gate its
temperature-fallback ladder. Studied how a flagged window can be re-decoded
via the sampling regime (beam_size=1, sampling_topk=0, sampling_temperature>0)
at rising temperatures, a control structure no prior iter built.
what_i_learned:
The ledger has mined every field generate() RETURNS (scores, no_speech_prob,
N-best sequences_ids, align's text_token_probs) but never the canonical
degeneracy detector that lives outside the return surface: a pure post-process
on the decoded string. A window collapsed into repeated/hallucinated text
compresses far past ~2.4 while natural Korean speech stays under it, so
compression-ratio + avg_logprob<-1.0 reconstructs Whisper's fallback gate with
no new backend call, and the sampling re-decode is the unused escape hatch the
beam regime cannot produce.
hypothesis:
Keep beam search as the temperature-0 primary decode (untouched on the healthy
substitution/coverage windows), but when a window trips avg_logprob<-1.0 OR
compression_ratio>2.4, climb the sampling-temperature ladder (0.2..1.0) and
accept the first attempt that stops degenerating, keeping the best-scoring
attempt as floor. This is self-budgeting (only flagged windows pay extra
passes) and targets the hallucination tail (hal 0.18, both focus files are
hallucination_hit guard violations) without disturbing substitution.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s suppress_tokens decoding kwarg — named in the frozen backend
docstring ("suppress_blank, suppress_tokens, …") but never used or recorded in
the ledger. Studied how a token-id list passed here constrains the decode
vocabulary, and how -1 expands to the model's default non-speech set, so a
custom list can be appended without losing the built-in suppression.
what_i_learned:
suppress_tokens is a token-level decode constraint distinct from every scalar
(beam/patience/temperature/penalty) and every rerank (align, MBR) tried so far:
it removes ids from the candidate distribution before search. Because Whisper's
vocab is byte-level BPE, Korean Hangul shares 3-byte fragments with CJK, and
those fragment tokens decode to U+FFFD — so only WHOLE-character CJK/kana
tokens can be safely identified (decode([id]) is entirely in CJK/kana ranges).
Suppressing exactly those can only delete wrong-script output, never a token
Korean needs. -1 must be prepended to keep the backend default suppression.
hypothesis:
Dominant axis is substitution (58%) on degraded phone-band Korean, where
large-v3-turbo is known to emit hanja/kana in place of Hangul. I keep the
iter11 beam+align pipeline unchanged and add suppress_tokens=[-1]+<pure
CJK/kana ids> to the generate() call, forcing the decoder's probability mass
onto in-script (Korean/Latin/digit) tokens and eliminating an entire class of
cross-script substitutions at zero coverage cost.

capability_investigated:
model.align()'s WhisperAlignmentResult.alignments field — the list of
(text_token_index, audio_frame_index) pairs returned alongside
text_token_probs. The ledger (iter10/11) only ever read text_token_probs and
threw alignments away; this is the per-token TIME map, not the confidence map.
what_i_learned:
align() returns alignments parallel to text_token_probs: each entry maps a
text token to its audio frame index at the ~50fps encoder rate (num_frames
units), so max(frame)/_FRAMES_PER_SEC is the audio-time end of the last
transcribed word — a finer seam signal than the last timestamp token, which
is quantized to 0.02s grid and can land in trailing silence past the final
word (re-decoded as boundary hallucination next window) or be absent.
hypothesis:
Replace the timestamp-token cursor advance with align()'s word-level
alignments: advance pos to the last text token's audio frame so each window
is cut exactly at the end of speech, removing the silence overshoot that
seeds boundary substitutions/hallucination, with the old last-ts rule kept as
fallback when a window has no alignable text.

capability_investigated:
model.detect_language(features) — the third method on the live
ctranslate2.models.Whisper that load() returns. The ledger has only ever
called generate() and align(); this method has never been invoked. It runs
the encoder plus one decoder step and returns, per batch item, a ranked list
of (language_token, probability) pairs.
what_i_learned:
detect_language() is reachable on the frozen model object and yields a
per-window language posterior (dict of "<|ko|>"/"<|en|>"/... -> prob) that
generate()'s sequences_ids/scores/no_speech_prob and align()'s
text_token_probs cannot isolate — those all assume the language is already
fixed to the forced <|ko|> prompt. It is the only surface signal that scores
whether a window is Korean speech at all, distinct from the no_speech_prob
scalar (iter14) which measures silence, not wrong-language content.
hypothesis:
Forcing <|ko|> on non-Korean/non-speech windows (noise, hold-music, ring-back
in the high-silence focus files carrying the hallucination_hit flags) emits
hallucinated Korean scored as substitution+insertion. Gating each window on
p_ko >= 0.1 (low threshold so acoustically-poor real Korean is never dropped)
before the beam+align decode drops exactly those windows, attacking the
hallucination axis on the two guard_violation focus files while bounding added
deletion risk and saving decode cost on skipped windows.

capability_investigated:
The parallel sequences_ids returned under the sampling regime (beam_size=1,
sampling_topk=0, sampling_temperature>0, num_hypotheses=N) examined as a
per-POSITION structure rather than the whole-string set iter13 reduced to a
single medoid edit-distance.
what_i_learned:
Whole-string MBR (iter13) collapses each hypothesis to one scalar distance, so
it can only select an existing sample — it discards where the diverse pool
agrees vs disagrees position-by-position. That positional-agreement signal is
already in sequences_ids (no new backend call); aligning the samples and
voting per word slot can synthesize a string cleaner than any single
hypothesis, which a re-ranking selector structurally cannot.
hypothesis:
Decode each window with the sampling pool, anchor on the highest-score hyp
(it drives the timestamp cursor and ROVER reference so coverage/length are
fixed), then ROVER word-level majority-vote over one-for-one substitution
spans aligned to the anchor. When N samples mis-hear a domain term N different
ways the modal rendering wins token-by-token, attacking the 58% substitution
axis directly.

capability_investigated:
The raw audio array passed to processor() before mel extraction — an INPUT
axis, not a decode kwarg. Studied whether the WhisperProcessor /
feature-extractor front-end applies any per-utterance loudness/gain
normalization, or passes the waveform's absolute amplitude straight through
to the log-mel spectrogram the encoder consumes.
what_i_learned:
Whisper's log-mel front-end applies a FIXED log normalization
((log_spec+4)/4, clamped) but no per-utterance AGC, so absolute waveform gain
survives into the mel energy the encoder sees. The eval batch spans
rms_db_mean -26 to -41 dB (per-file diagnosis), meaning calls reach the model
at very different drive levels — a never-conditioned-on input axis that the
decode-side surface (beam, align, suppress_tokens, detect_language) cannot
touch because it acts after feature extraction.
hypothesis:
Peak-normalize the whole call once to a target amplitude (0.95) before
windowing, guarding near-silent audio so the noise floor is not amplified.
Standardizing the input loudness aligns the mel distribution with what the
model expects and attacks substitutions on quiet / phone-band windows that
under-drive the encoder — the dominant axis (sub 58%) that decode knobs left
untouched.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> context slot used as a GLOBAL call-derived vocabulary
prime, built from a frequency table over a cheap greedy first-pass decode of
the whole call — a two-pass structure no prior iter built. Distinct from
iter5 (rolling one-window-back text) and iter8 (fixed external glossary).
what_i_learned:
generate() can be run twice over the same audio with the second pass's
prompt conditioned on the first pass's output: the most-frequent eojeols of
the pass-1 transcript form a compact (<=200-token) domain-vocabulary prime
that fits inside Whisper's 448-token decoder context alongside the sot
sequence, so the call's own recurring terms/names can bias every pass-2
window's token distribution without per-window state — a global prior the
isolated per-window decode structurally lacks.
hypothesis:
Substitution (58%) is idiosyncratic domain-term mis-recognition decoded
inconsistently across isolated windows. Priming every pass-2 window on the
call's own high-frequency vocabulary should stabilize those spellings call-
wide, attacking substitution; runtime stays in budget by dropping the
near-duplicate-N-best align() rerank to pay for the greedy pass-1.
